title: Automate the bisect and walk away
summary: Write a test script that exits 0 for good and 1 for bad, hand it to git bisect run, and let it find the culprit across two hundred commits without you.
mental_model: `bisect run <cmd>` replaces you. Exit 0 means good, 1–124 means bad, 125 means skip, and anything above 127 aborts. Your only job is writing a script that returns the right code.

commit.message: Add a cache size limit constant
Evict the whole cache when it fills up

steps.title: Write the test as a script
steps.why: The script is the whole contract. This one puts more entries than the limit and checks an early key survived — a behaviour regression rather than a crash, which is where bisect earns its keep.

write.content:
#!/bin/sh
# exit 0 = good, 1 = bad, 125 = cannot test this commit

[ -f cache.py ] || exit 125

python - <<'PY'
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import cache

for i in range(150):
    cache.put('k%d' % i, i)

if cache.get('k0') is None:
    sys.exit(1)   # regression: early entries were evicted
sys.exit(0)
PY

steps.expect: Exit 1 — the regression is present on HEAD.

steps.title: Keep the script out of the bisect's way
steps.why: Bisect checks out old commits, which do not contain your test script. Committing it would change every checkout; leaving it untracked and ignored means it survives every checkout untouched.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Ignore the local bisect script"

steps.expect: The script present on disk but untracked and ignored.

steps.title: Verify both endpoints
steps.why: Same discipline as a manual bisect: prove the tag is good and HEAD is bad before starting. An unverified endpoint is the main way an automated bisect produces a confident wrong answer.

steps.title: Hand the whole search to git
steps.why: One command. Git checks out each midpoint, runs the script, reads the exit code, and keeps going until it converges — then prints the first bad commit and its diff.
steps.expect: A few automated steps, then '<sha> is the first bad commit'.

verify.label: bisect run found the eviction commit automatically
verify.hint: git bisect start HEAD <good-tag> && git bisect run sh bisect_test.sh

steps.title: Read the log it produced
steps.why: `bisect log` records every decision. Paste it into the incident ticket and anyone can replay the search exactly with `git bisect replay`.
steps.expect: A reproducible transcript of the search.

steps.title: Reset and fix the actual bug
steps.why: Bisect found it; fixing it is ordinary work. Evicting one entry rather than clearing the whole cache is the correct behaviour, and the test script now passes.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Evict one entry instead of clearing the cache"

verify.label: the bisect was reset before committing the fix

steps.title: Turn the script into a real test
steps.why: The script that found the bug is a regression test. Committing it means the next person to write this bug is told immediately, rather than bisecting for it in a year.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Add a regression test for cache eviction"

verify.label: the bisect script became a committed regression test
the regression bisect found is fixed
verify.hint: git bisect run sh bisect_test.sh finds it, then fix it normally

verify.label: a regression test was committed so it cannot come back
the throwaway bisect script stayed untracked
verify.hint: ignore it so checking out old commits does not disturb it

pitfalls: Exit code 125 means 'cannot test this commit' and makes bisect skip it. Use it for commits that do not build, or bisect will call them bad.
The test script must live outside the repository or be ignored. If it is tracked, checking out an old commit removes or changes it.
Exit codes above 127 abort the whole bisect. A script that returns 255 on error will stop the search rather than marking the commit bad.
`git bisect start HEAD <good>` sets both endpoints in one command — bad first, then good.
For a performance regression, make the script compare against a threshold and exit 1 when exceeded. Bisect does not care what 'bad' means.
cheatsheet: let a script answer every step
